title: Next.js Development
excerpt: Next.js applications with a clear App Router structure, fast pages, and a backend that is not bolted on later.

seo.title: Next.js Development | Mohit Walia
seo.description: Next.js applications with a clear App Router structure, fast pages, and a backend that is not bolted on later.

hero.heading: Next.js development for products that need to stay fast.
hero.subtitle: I use the App Router, server rendering, and TypeScript so the product is quick to load and straightforward to extend.

overview: Next.js is the default I reach for when a product needs marketing pages, an application, and a deployment story in one place. This service is the build itself: routes, data, UI, and release.
problem: Teams adopt Next.js and then fight it. Client components everywhere, data fetched twice, and a folder structure nobody wants to open six months later.
solution: I keep server components as the default, put client code only where the browser is required, and structure routes so a new page has an obvious home.

features.title: App Router structure
features.detail: Layouts, loading states, and route groups that match how the product is organized.

features.title: Typed data boundaries
features.detail: The shape of the data is explicit where it enters the UI.

features.title: Deployed on Vercel
features.detail: Preview deployments so you can review a change before it is the live site.

process.title: Discovery
process.detail: We pin down the outcome, the constraints, and what the first release has to do.

process.title: Planning
process.detail: I turn that into a scope, a sequence, and the technical approach.

process.title: Development
process.detail: I build in small slices you can review, on the stack this service uses.

process.title: Testing
process.detail: We check the flows that matter before anything is treated as finished.

process.title: Launch
process.detail: I ship it, watch the first days, and leave you with a clear way to change it.

benefits.title: Less client JavaScript
benefits.detail: Pages stay light because the server does the work it should.

benefits.title: Reviews are concrete
benefits.detail: You click through a preview, not a slide.

benefits.title: A path for the next feature
benefits.detail: New routes follow the same pattern as the first ones.

faqs.question: Can you join a Next.js codebase that already exists?
faqs.answer: Yes. I start by reading how routes and data work today, then change the part you hired me for without a rewrite you did not ask for.

faqs.question: Do you use the App Router?
faqs.answer: Yes, for new work. If the project is still on the older pages router, I will say so before moving anything.
